### LockModule

File: `libs/infrastructure/lock/lock.module.ts`

Description: LockModule provides distributed locking infrastructure. Default priority: Redis (primary) → PostgreSQL (fallback). If Redis is unavailable, all lock operations automatically fall back to PG advisory locks. Example : // Default — Redis primary + PG fallback LockModule.forRoot() \_\_\_COMPODOC\_EMPTY\_LINE\_\_\_ // Custom adapters LockModule.forRoot({ adapters: \[redisLockAdapter, postgresLockAdapter\], })

Methods:
- `createDefaultAdapters(): LockAdapter[]` — Creates the default adapter chain: Redis (primary) → PostgreSQL (fallback).
- `forRoot(config?: Partial<LockManagerConfig>): { module: typeof LockModule; providers: {}; exports: {}; }` — Configure the lock module with custom adapters and options. Default: Redis primary → PostgreSQL fallback.
- `getAdapterStatus(): Promise<{ primary: string; healthy: boolean }>` — Get the active adapter status for startup logging.
- `getRedisLockAdapter(): RedisLockAdapter | null` — Get the RedisLockAdapter instance (used to configure it with a Redis client after DI is ready).
- `onApplicationShutdown(): any`
- `onModuleInit(): void`

## Services / Injectables

### AdminAuthService

File: `src/modules/auth/service/admin-auth.service.ts`

Description: AdminAuthService — owns the admin password-reset flow. Unlike the user OTP flow, admins reset via a one-time link : requestPasswordReset(email) issues a single-use token (persisted in the otp table with purpose = PASSWORD\_RESET ) and e-mails a link. resetPassword({ token, password }) validates + consumes that token, sets the new password and revokes every refresh token. The token is stored in the dedicated OTP table (reused as a generic one-time-token store) so the link is single-use, expirable and revocable.

Methods:
- `buildResetUrl(token: string): string`
- `requestPasswordReset(email: string): Promise<AdminResetPasswordResponseDto>` — Step 1 — issue a reset link to the admin's e-mail. Anti-enumeration: always reports success and only acts when an active admin with that e-mail exists, so the response never reveals whether the address is registered.
- `resetPassword(dto: AdminResetPasswordDto): Promise<AdminResetPasswordResponseDto>` — Step 2 — consume the token from the link and set the new password. Revokes all refresh tokens so every existing admin session is logged out.

### ApiKeyService

File: `src/modules/api-key/api-key.service.ts`

Properties:
- `logger: unknown = new Logger(ApiKeyService.name)`

Methods:
- `activate(id: string): Promise<void>`
- `create(data: { name: string; description?: string; scopes?: string[]; expiresAt?: Date }): Promise<{ apiKey: ApiKey; rawKey: string }>` — Tạo API key mới. Trả về raw key (chỉ hiển thị 1 lần).
- `delete(id: string): Promise<void>`
- `findAll(): Promise<ApiKey[]>`
- `generateRawKey(): string`
- `hasAllScopes(apiKey: ApiKey, requiredScopes: string[]): boolean`
- `hashKey(rawKey: string): string`
- `hasScope(apiKey: ApiKey, requiredScope: string): boolean` — Check xem API key có scope cần thiết không. Nếu scopes = null → full access (không giới hạn).
- `revoke(id: string): Promise<void>`
- `validate(rawKey: string): Promise<ApiKeyValidationResult>` — Validate API key từ header. Trả về thông tin service nếu hợp lệ.

### AuthRepository

File: `src/modules/auth/auth.repository.ts`

Description: Repository\_Layer for the OTP aggregate inside the Auth module. Responsibilities: Encapsulate every read/write against the otp table. Inherit the standard BaseRepository contract ( findById , findByIdOrFail , save , softDelete , count ). Expose OTP-specific query/command methods that the existing AuthService performs directly on Repository\<OTPEntity\> today. Constraints (per design / Requirements 3.1, 3.2, 12.1, 12.3, 12.4): MUST inject Repository\<OTPEntity\> via @InjectRepository . MUST NOT inject services from other modules — cross-module access (e.g. looking up the User) is handled in the Service layer. MUST NOT inject EventEmitter2 — emitting domain events is the Service layer's responsibility. MUST NOT enforce business validation (token expiry, retry caps, is-locked checks all stay in the Service layer). The entityName ("otp") is used by findByIdOrFail to throw a import('@nestjs/common').NotFoundException with the i18n key 'otp.not\_found' .

Properties:
- `entityName: string = 'otp'`
- `repo: Repository<TEntity>` — TypeORM repository injected by the subclass.

Methods:
- `findActiveByUserId(userId: string): Promise<OTPEntity | null>` — Find the OTP row currently associated with a user. The userId column is unique, so at most one row is returned. Soft-deleted rows are excluded by default. Note: this method intentionally does not filter on isUsed or expiredAt — verifying that the OTP is still valid (expiry, retry counter, isUsed flag) is the Service layer's job.
- `findByIdentifier(identifier: string, purpose?: OtpPurpose): Promise<OTPEntity | null>` — Look up an OTP row by its public identifier. When purpose is provided the lookup is constrained to that purpose — this matches the findOne({ where: { identifier, purpose } }) calls in AuthService.verifyLogin and AuthService.adminResetPassword . Returns null when no row matches.
- `findByIdentifierWithDeleted(identifier: string): Promise<OTPEntity | null>` — Look up an OTP row by identifier, including soft-deleted rows. Replicates the findOne({ where: { identifier }, withDeleted: true }) behaviour used by AuthService.resendOtp to find the previous OTP even after a soft delete.
- `hardDelete(id: string): Promise<void>` — Hard-delete an OTP row by id. Used by AuthService when an OTP is fully consumed (successful verify) or invalidated (max retries reached, account locked) — i.e. the row should not be recoverable.
- `incrementRetry(id: string, retry: number): Promise<void>` — Increment the retry counter on a specific OTP row. Callers compute the next retry value ( current + 1 ) so the operation is a direct UPDATE — the repository is not concerned with retry caps.
- `insertOtp(data: Omit<UpsertOtpInput, "userId">, meta?: Record<string, any>): Promise<void>`
- `markUsed(id: string, expiredAt: Date): Promise<void>` — Mark an OTP as consumed and extend its window so the caller can complete the follow-up step (typically the password-reset flow's "set new password" call). The repository performs the UPDATE only — deciding when an OTP becomes "used" is a service concern.
- `softDeleteByIdentifier(identifier: string): Promise<void>` — Soft-delete an OTP row by its public identifier. Mirrors a softDelete({ identifier }) call so the Service layer can avoid loading the row first when the identifier is the only known key.
- `upsertOtp(data: UpsertOtpInput): Promise<void>` — Insert-or-replace the OTP row for a user. The unique constraint on userId drives the conflict resolution — if the user already has an OTP row it is overwritten (same behaviour as the existing AuthService.generateOTP flow).
- `count(options?: FindManyOptions<TEntity>): Promise<number>` — Count rows that match the given options. The options shape mirrors TypeORM's FindManyOptions.
- `findById(id: string): Promise<TEntity | null>` — Look up an entity by its primary id. Returns null when the id does not exist (no exception thrown).
- `findByIdOrFail(id: string): Promise<TEntity>` — Same as findById but throws NotFoundException with an i18n key ( {entity}.not\_found ) when the id does not exist.
- `save(data: Partial<TEntity>): Promise<TEntity>` — Persist a partial entity. Implementations may either INSERT a new row (when id is absent) or UPDATE an existing row.
- `softDelete(id: string): Promise<void>` — Soft-delete the entity with the given id (sets deleted\_at ).

### AuthService

File: `src/modules/auth/service/auth.service.ts`

Description: AuthService — Complex\_Business\_Service for the Auth module. Owns registration, login (user + admin), JWT issuance and account-state validation. OTP concerns have been extracted to OtpService. Persistence is delegated to UserRepository — owns the users table (cross-module DI; UserModule exports UserRepository ).

Properties:
- `config: ConfigService`
- `jwtService: JwtService`

Methods:
- `adminLogin(dto: AdminLoginRequestDto): Promise<LoginResponseDto>`
- `createToken(data: UserEntity): IToken`
- `createUser(userRegisterDto: RegisterDto, social?: SocialRegisterIdentity): Promise<UserEntity>`
- `getUserInfo(id: string | null): Promise<MyInfoResponseDto>`
- `issueSession(user: UserEntity): Promise<LoginResponseDto>` — Mint a full login session (access + refresh) for an already-validated user and shape it as a LoginResponseDto.
- `login(dto: LoginRequestDto): Promise<OtpSentResponseDto | LoginResponseDto>` — Login step 1. Verifies the credentials, then branches by role: parent : an e-mail OTP second factor is required, so instead of a session this returns the OTP challenge { identifier, expiredAt } . The client completes login via POST /auth/otp/verify (see OtpService.verifyOtp → LOGIN\_VERIFY branch). other roles (admin/caregiver): a session is issued immediately.
- `registerParentInfo(userId: string, dto: UpsertParentProfileInfoDto): Promise<MyInfoResponseDto>` — Parent onboarding step ("đăng ký thông tin trẻ"). The registration flow only creates the user ; the parent\_profile row is born here, the first place that owns the children data. Idempotent — resubmitting updates the same row. Returns the refreshed getUserInfo so the client sees requireAction flip to NONE once the profile exists.
- `resetPassword(dto: ResetPasswordDto): Promise<ResetPasswordResponseDto>` — Final step of the "forgot password" flow. Trusts the short-lived token issued by OtpService.verifyOtp (server-signed, carries the OTP-verified e-mail) instead of re-checking the OTP. Sets the new password and revokes every refresh token so all existing sessions are logged out. Returns success: true regardless of whether the e-mail maps to a real account, so the endpoint does not leak account existence.
- `resolveRequireAction(id: string | null, user: UserEntity | null): Promise<RequireAction>` — Decide whether the client still owes an onboarding step: no account yet (anonymous / social sign-up not finished) → must register; a parent without a parent\_profile row → must complete the children info step (see registerParentInfo); otherwise nothing is required. Sitter onboarding has its own (later) flow, so other roles return NONE .
- `socialLogin(dto: SocialLoginDto): Promise<SocialLoginResponseDto>`
- `userRegister(dto: RegisterDto, social?: SocialRegisterIdentity): Promise<LoginResponseDto>`

### ChildrenService

File: `src/modules/children/children.service.ts`

Methods:
- `assertComplete(child: Child): Promise<void>` — Ném 422 kèm danh sách field còn thiếu nếu hồ sơ chưa đủ điều kiện hoàn tất.
- `getMany(req: CrudRequest, query?: RequestGetManyChildrenDto): unknown`
- `submit(id: string, userId: string): Promise<Child>` — Hoàn tất hồ sơ nháp: validate đầy đủ field bắt buộc (group COMPLETE), pass thì chuyển status sang COMPLETE. Scope theo userId để phụ huynh chỉ submit được hồ sơ của chính mình.
- `updateForOwner(req: CrudRequest, dto: Child, id: string, userId: string): Promise<Child>` — Cập nhật có kiểm soát trạng thái: Hồ sơ DRAFT: sửa tự do (validate relaxed do crud lo ở group UPDATE). Hồ sơ COMPLETE: validate đầy đủ trên bản đã merge — không cho sửa thành thiếu/rỗng; status giữ nguyên COMPLETE. Scope theo userId để phụ huynh chỉ sửa hồ sơ của chính mình.

### ConversationService

File: `src/modules/conversation/conversation.service.ts`

Properties:
- `logger: unknown = new Logger(ConversationService.name)`

Methods:
- `addMember(userId: string, groupId: string, dto: AddMemberDto): Promise<void>` — Add a member to a group conversation. Validates the acting user has owner/admin role Checks group capacity (max 10 active participants) Handles re-add of soft-deleted participant (restore record) Rejects if user is already an active participant Generates system message Emits MemberAddedEvent Requirements: 2.1, 2.2, 2.6, 2.7, 2.8
- `batchIncrementUnreadCounts(groupId: string, userIds: string[]): Promise<void>` — Batch increment unread counts for multiple users via Redis pipeline. Uses a single Redis round-trip for all INCR + EXPIRE commands.
- `cacheGroupInfo(group: Conversation): Promise<void>` — Cache group info in Redis.
- `createGroup(userId: string, dto: CreateGroupDto): Promise<ConversationResponseDto>` — Create a new group conversation. Deduplicates participantIds Validates total count (5-10 including creator) Validates all participant IDs exist as active users Creates Conversation + Participant records in a transaction Emits GroupCreatedEvent for Socket.IO broadcast Requirements: 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 1.4, 1.6, 1.7, 1.8
- `dissolveGroup(userId: string, groupId: string): Promise<void>` — Dissolve a group conversation (owner only). Validates the acting user is the owner Persists system message indicating dissolution Soft-deletes all participants and the conversation Messages are preserved (not soft-deleted) Emits GroupDissolvedEvent Requirements: 7.4, 7.5, 7.7, 7.8
- `dissolveGroupInternal(manager: any, group: Conversation, groupId: string): Promise<void>` — Internal helper: Dissolve a group (soft-delete conversation and all participants). Messages are preserved (not soft-deleted).
- `findExistingByClientMessageId(groupId: string, senderId: string, clientMessageId: string): Promise<unknown | null>` — Find an existing message by clientMessageId for deduplication. Queries Message WHERE conversation\_id = groupId AND sender\_id = senderId AND client\_message\_id = clientMessageId. Returns the message response DTO if found, null otherwise. Requirements: 3.13, 3.14
- `getBatchTotalUnreadCounts(userIds: string[]): Promise<Map<string, number>>` — Batch get total unread counts for multiple users. Uses a single GROUP BY query instead of N individual SUM queries. Returns Map\<userId, totalUnreadCount\>. Requirements: real-time total unread badge for multiple recipients
- `getCachedGroupInfo(groupId: string): Promise<Record | null>` — Get cached group info from Redis. Returns null on cache miss or Redis unavailability.
- `getGroupDetail(userId: string, groupId: string): Promise<ConversationDetailResponseDto>` — Get group detail with participant list and avatar presigned GET URL. Validates participant membership Joins participants with UserEntity for display names Generates presigned GET URL for avatar via StorageService Returns ConversationDetailResponseDto Requirements: 6.6
- `getMessages(userId: string, groupId: string, dto: GetMessagesDto): Promise<PaginatedMessagesResponseDto>` — Get message history for a group conversation with cursor-based pagination. Validates participant membership Queries messages WHERE conversation\_id = groupId AND id \< cursor (if provided) ORDER BY id DESC, LIMIT dto.limit Includes sender display name by joining with UserEntity Includes attachment metadata by joining with MessageAttachment Computes nextCursor and hasMore (queries limit+1 to check) Requirements: 5.1, 5.2, 5.3, 5.4, 5.5, 5.6, 5.7
- `getTotalUnreadCount(userId: string): Promise<{ totalUnreadCount: number }>` — Get total unread message count across all conversations for a user. Sums the unread\_count column from group\_participant for the user. This is a fast SUM query on indexed column (user\_id + deleted\_at). Requirements: total unread badge across all conversations
- `getUploadUrl(userId: string, groupId: string, dto: UploadFileDto): Promise<PresignedUploadResponseDto>` — Get a presigned upload URL for file attachment in a group conversation. Validates participant membership Determines file size limit based on content type (10MB for image/\*, 100MB otherwise) Delegates to StorageService for presigned POST URL with content-length-range condition Returns the upload URL, file key, and form fields Requirements: 4.1, 4.5, 4.6, 4.7, 4.8
- `getUserGroups(userId: string, dto: GetGroupsDto): Promise<PaginatedConversationsResponseDto>` — Get the list of group conversations for a user. Queries active Conversations where user is an active participant Joins last message for preview (truncated to 100 chars) Includes unread count from participant record (with Redis fallback) Sorts by COALESCE(last\_message\_at, created\_at) DESC Cursor-based pagination using the group's Snowflake ID Requirements: 9.1, 9.2, 9.3, 9.4, 9.5
- `incrementUnreadCount(groupId: string, userId: string): Promise<void>` — Increment unread count for a user in a group via Redis INCR. Used when a new message is sent. Sets TTL to prevent unbounded key growth.
- `invalidateGroupInfoCache(groupId: string): Promise<void>` — Invalidate the group info cache. Called when group metadata is updated.
- `invalidateParticipantsCache(groupId: string): Promise<void>` — Invalidate the participants cache for a group. Called when members are added, removed, or leave.
- `invalidateUserGroupsCache(userId: string): Promise<void>` — Invalidate the user's group list cache. Called when a user is added to or removed from a group.
- `leaveGroup(userId: string, groupId: string): Promise<void>` — Leave a group conversation. Soft-deletes the participant record Handles ownership transfer if owner leaves (earliest admin, then earliest member) Auto-dissolves group if remaining active participants \< 2 Generates system message Emits MemberLeftEvent (and GroupDissolvedEvent if auto-dissolved) Requirements: 7.1, 7.2, 7.3, 7.6
- `markDelivered(messageId: string, recipientId: string, groupId: string): Promise<void>` — Mark a message as delivered for a specific recipient. Called when the recipient's device acknowledges receipt via WebSocket. Updates the MessageStatus record from SENT → DELIVERED. Emits MessageDeliveredEvent to notify the sender. Requirements: real-time delivery acknowledgment
- `markRead(userId: string, groupId: string, messageIds?: string[]): Promise<void>` — Mark messages as read for a specific user in a group. Called when the user opens a conversation via WebSocket. Updates all MessageStatus records from SENT/DELIVERED → READ. Emits MessageReadEvent for each message to notify the senders. Requirements: real-time read acknowledgment
- `removeMember(userId: string, groupId: string, targetUserId: string): Promise<void>` — Remove a member from a group conversation. Validates the acting user has owner/admin role Validates role hierarchy (admin cannot remove owner/admin) Soft-deletes the participant record Generates system message Emits MemberRemovedEvent Requirements: 2.3, 2.6, 2.9
- `resetUnreadCount(userId: string, groupId: string): Promise<void>` — Reset unread count for a user in a group (conversation opened). Updates both Redis and DB. Requirements: 9.6
- `sendMessage(userId: string, groupId: string, dto: SendMessageDto): Promise<MessageResponseDto & { isNew: boolean }>` — Send a message to a group conversation. Validates participant membership Validates clientMessageId (required, UUID format) Performs deduplication check (returns existing message if duplicate) Validates content (1-5000 chars for text, non-empty content or fileKeys) Validates fileKeys exist in uploaded\_file records Persists Message and MessageAttachment records Commits file keys via StorageService Updates conversation last\_message\_at/last\_message\_id Increments unread counts for other participants via Redis Emits NewMessageEvent for Socket.IO broadcast Requirements: 3.1, 3.2, 3.3, 3.5, 3.6, 3.7, 3.8, 3.9, 3.10, 3.12, 3.13, 3.14, 4.2, 4.3, 4.4, 9.5
- `setUnreadCount(groupId: string, userId: string, count: number): Promise<void>` — Set the unread count for a user in a group via Redis. Used for explicit reset (conversation-opened).
- `transferOwnership(manager: any, groupId: string, group: Conversation): Promise<void>` — Internal helper: Transfer ownership to the next eligible participant. Priority: earliest admin by joined\_at, then earliest member by joined\_at.
- `updateGroup(userId: string, groupId: string, dto: UpdateGroupDto): Promise<ConversationResponseDto>` — Update group information (name and/or avatar). Validates the acting user has owner/admin role Trims and validates name (1-100 chars, non-blank after trim) Validates avatarFileKey exists in uploaded\_file records Persists changes Commits avatar file key via StorageService Generates system messages for each change Emits GroupUpdatedEvent Requirements: 6.1, 6.2, 6.3, 6.4, 6.5

### FcmDispatcher

Description: Firebase Cloud Messaging dispatcher. Sends push notifications via firebase-admin SDK. Splits device tokens into batches of 500 (FCM multicast limit). Uses in-memory TokenBucket to enforce rate limits (default: 10 req/s). Never throws — returns DispatchResult with success/error.

- `logger: unknown = new Logger(FcmDispatcher.name)`

Methods:

- `dispatch(payload: FcmPayload): unknown` — Dispatch a push notification to one or more devices. Splits tokens into batches ≤ 500 (FCM limit). Rate-limits via TokenBucket (one token per batch). If FCM is not configured, logs and returns success (no-op mode).
- `onModuleInit(): any`

### HttpClientService

File: `libs/infrastructure/http-client/http-client.service.ts`

Properties:
- `config: Required<any>`
- `logger: LoggingService`
- `requestInterceptors: RequestInterceptor[] = []`
- `responseInterceptors: ResponseInterceptor[] = []`

Methods:
- `addRequestInterceptor(interceptor: RequestInterceptor): void`
- `addResponseInterceptor(interceptor: ResponseInterceptor): void`
- `buildHeaders(body: unknown, overrides?: Record<string, string>): Record<string, string>` — Merge default, body-derived and per-request headers. Precedence (low → high): config defaults → body content-type → caller headers.
- `buildUrl(url: string, params?: Record<string, string | number | boolean | undefined>): string`
- `delete(url: string, options?: RequestOptions): Promise<HttpResponse<T>>`
- `executeRequest(method: string, fullUrl: string, body: unknown, options: RequestOptions | undefined, timeoutMs: number, shouldThrow: boolean): Promise<HttpResponse<T>>`
- `get(url: string, options?: RequestOptions): Promise<HttpResponse<T>>`
- `getStream(url: string, options?: RequestOptions): Promise<HttpStreamResponse>` — GET request that returns a readable stream. Useful for proxying file downloads, SSE, or large responses. Example : // Pipe to Express response (file download proxy) const { stream, headers } = await this.http.getStream('/files/report.pdf'); res.set('Content-Type', headers\['content-type'\]); Readable.fromWeb(stream).pipe(res); Example : // SSE forwarding const { stream } = await this.http.getStream('/events', { headers: { Accept: 'text/event-stream' }, timeout: 0, // no timeout for SSE });
- `isRetryable(error: Error): boolean`
- `patch(url: string, body?: unknown, options?: RequestOptions): Promise<HttpResponse<T>>`
- `post(url: string, body?: unknown, options?: RequestOptions): Promise<HttpResponse<T>>`
- `postStream(url: string, body?: unknown, options?: RequestOptions): Promise<HttpStreamResponse>` — POST request that returns a readable stream. Useful for AI/LLM streaming responses, chunked uploads, etc.
- `put(url: string, body?: unknown, options?: RequestOptions): Promise<HttpResponse<T>>`
- `request(method: string, url: string, body?: unknown, options?: RequestOptions): Promise<HttpResponse<T>>`
- `requestStream(method: string, url: string, body?: unknown, options?: RequestOptions): Promise<HttpStreamResponse>`
- `serializeBody(body: unknown): { body: BodyInit | undefined; contentType?: string }` — Serialize a request body into a fetch-compatible BodyInit . Plain objects are JSON-encoded (default). Already-encoded bodies — URLSearchParams (form-urlencoded), strings, Buffers/typed arrays, Blobs and streams — are passed through untouched so callers can send form-urlencoded or binary payloads. The returned contentType is applied by buildHeaders unless the caller sets its own Content-Type .
- `sleep(ms: number): Promise<void>`
- `toNodeStream(webStream: ReadableStream<Uint8Array>): Readable` — Convert a Web ReadableStream to a Node.js Readable stream. Convenience helper for piping to Express/NestJS responses. Example : const { stream } = await this.http.getStream('/file.zip'); const nodeStream = this.http.toNodeStream(stream); nodeStream.pipe(res);

### MailScheduler

File: `src/modules/email/mail.scheduler.ts`

Description: Recovery-only scheduler for the email module. When BullMQ/Redis is healthy, emails are dispatched immediately. When Redis is down, this scheduler picks up stuck PENDING records. Uses @DistributedLock to ensure only one instance runs recovery, with automatic Redis → PostgreSQL advisory lock fallback. BullMQ future: when BullMQ worker handles retries, this scheduler only needs to recover truly stuck messages (PENDING \> N minutes).

Properties:
- `cleanupDays: number = 30` — Days after which sent/permanently-failed records are cleaned up
- `logger: unknown = new Logger(MailScheduler.name)`
- `stuckThresholdMinutes: number = 2` — Minutes after which a PENDING record is considered "stuck"

Methods:
- `cleanup(): Promise<void>` — Cleanup job: removes old sent and permanently-failed records. Runs daily at 3:00 AM.
- `dispatchOne(record: any): Promise<void>`
- `recoverStuckEmails(): Promise<void>` — Recovery job: finds emails stuck in PENDING state and dispatches them. Runs every 30 seconds with a distributed lock. Lock uses Redis (primary) → PostgreSQL advisory lock (fallback).

### MailService

File: `src/modules/email/mail.service.ts`

Description: Central mail service — orchestrates template validation, outbox persistence, and dispatch. EJS rendering is delegated to the dispatcher (SmtpEmailDispatcher or BullMqEmailDispatcher), keeping the HTTP server lightweight. Public API: sendByTemplate(templateName, to, data) — validate → outbox → dispatch raw sendCustomEmail(to, subject, body) — outbox → dispatch pre-rendered Event handlers: Dynamically registered via EventEmitter2.on() for each MAIL\_EVENT\_MAP entry. Fire-and-forget: errors are logged but never re-thrown.

Properties:
- `logger: unknown = new Logger(MailService.name)`

Methods:
- `handleMailEvent(event: any): Promise<void>` — Common handler for all mail events. Looks up template name from MAIL\_EVENT\_MAP (single source of truth). Delegates to sendByTemplate. Fire-and-forget: errors are logged, never re-thrown.
- `onModuleInit(): void` — Register dynamic @OnEvent handlers for each event in the registry. Uses EventEmitter2.on() instead of 8 separate @OnEvent decorators.
- `sendByTemplate(templateName: string, to: string, data: Record<string, unknown> = {}): Promise<void>` — Send an email using a DB-stored template. Flow: validate template → outbox(PENDING) → dispatch raw EmailJob. EJS rendering happens in the dispatcher (SmtpEmailDispatcher or Worker).
- `sendCustomEmail(to: string, subject: string, body: string): Promise<void>` — Send a raw email without a template. Still goes through outbox for durability.

### MemoryHealthIndicator

File: `src/modules/health/indicators/memory.health-indicator.ts`

Properties:
- `heapThreshold: number = 0.9` — Heap usage ratio threshold (0-1). If heapUsed / heapTotal exceeds this, status becomes degraded. Default: 0.9 (90%) — indicates memory leak, GC under pressure.
- `name: string = 'memory'`
- `rssThreshold: unknown = 450 * 1024 * 1024` — RSS threshold in bytes. If RSS exceeds this, status becomes degraded. Default: 450MB — typical for NestJS app. Adjust per env.

Methods:

- `computeTrend(): { warning?: string | undefined; direction: string; rssGrowthPercent: string; consecutiveGrowth: any; samplesAnalyzed: any; periodSeconds: number; } | undefined` — Compute memory trend from the monitor's sliding window. Answers: has memory been growing steadily, or was that just a spike?
- `formatBytes(bytes: number): string`

### NestLoggerAdapter

File: `libs/infrastructure/logging/nest-logger.adapter.ts`

Description: Adapter that bridges NestJS's built-in LoggerService interface to our Winston-backed LoggingService. Usage in main.ts: const adapter = new NestLoggerAdapter(); const app = await NestFactory.create(AppModule, { logger: adapter, bufferLogs: true }); const loggingService = app.get(LoggingService); adapter.setLoggingService(loggingService);

Properties:
- `loggingService: LoggingService | null = null`

Methods:
- `debug(message: any, context?: string): void` — Maps NestJS debug → LoggingService.debug
- `error(message: any, stack?: string, context?: string): void` — Maps NestJS error → LoggingService.error Includes stack trace in metadata when provided.
- `log(message: any, context?: string): void` — Maps NestJS log → LoggingService.info
- `setLoggingService(service: LoggingService): void` — Called after the DI container is ready to wire in the real LoggingService. Until this is called, all log calls fall back to process.stdout JSON lines.
- `stringify(message: any): string` — Converts any message value to a string. Objects are JSON-serialized; primitives are coerced via String().
- `verbose(message: any, context?: string): void` — Maps NestJS verbose → LoggingService.verbose
- `warn(message: any, context?: string): void` — Maps NestJS warn → LoggingService.warn
- `writeStdout(level: string, message: string, context: string, extra?: Record<string, unknown>): void` — Fallback writer used before the DI container is ready. Writes a single-line JSON record to process.stdout.

### OtpService

File: `src/modules/auth/service/otp.service.ts`

Description: OtpService — owns the OTP lifecycle for the Auth module. Extracted from AuthService. Only the OTP "identifier" concept and the persistence handle (AuthRepository) are kept here for now; the verification / resend business logic is intentionally left unimplemented and will be rewritten in this service.

Properties:
- `MaxOtpRetry: number`
- `OtpExpirationMinutes: number`

Methods:
- `consumeOtp(dto: VerifyOtpDto): Promise<OTPEntity>` — Validate an OTP attempt (existence, expiry, retry cap, code match) and consume it (hard-delete) on success, returning the matched row. Throws a BadRequestException on any failure — shared by every verify flow.
- `generateOTP(otpSize: number = 6): Promise<{ identifier: string; expiredAt: Date; otp: string; expires: number }>`
- `issueLoginSession(userId: string): Promise<VerifyOtpResponseDto>` — Mint a full login session (access + refresh) for the user behind a verified login OTP. Re-checks account state in case it changed between the password step and OTP verification.
- `resendOtp(identifier: string): Promise<OtpSentResponseDto>`
- `sendLoginOtp(user: UserEntity): Promise<OtpSentResponseDto>` — Issue + send a login OTP for an already-authenticated (email+password verified) user. The OTP is keyed on userId (unique → one live OTP per user) with purpose OtpPurpose.LOGIN\_VERIFY; the verify step loads the user back from userId to mint the session, so no PII is stored here.
- `sendOtp(email: string): Promise<OtpSentResponseDto>`
- `verifyOtp(dto: VerifyOtpDto): Promise<VerifyOtpResponseDto>`

### OutboxEmailService

File: `src/modules/email/outbox-email.service.ts`

Description: Outbox service for email. Extends BaseOutboxService with no overrides — all logic is inherited. When BullMQ is integrated, this service remains unchanged; only the dispatcher and worker change.

Properties:
- `logger: unknown = new Logger(this.constructor.name)`

Methods:
- `cleanup(days: unknown = DEFAULT_CLEANUP_DAYS): Promise<number>` — Delete old sent or permanently-failed records.
- `createPending(data: Partial<T>): Promise<T>` — Create a new pending outbox record.

- `getStuckPending(minutes: number): Promise<T[]>` — Get records stuck in PENDING state for longer than the specified duration. Used by the scheduler for recovery when BullMQ/Redis is unavailable.
- `markFailed(id: string, error: string, permanent: unknown = false, patch?: Partial<T>): Promise<void>` — Mark a record as failed. Example : Use for permanent errors: invalid email, token not registered. Default false → keeps PENDING for scheduler retry. saved even though dispatch failed so the row reflects what was built.
- `markSent(id: string, patch?: Partial<T>): Promise<void>` — Mark a record as successfully sent. Uses TypeORM increment() — safe from SQL injection.

### PushScheduler

File: `src/modules/push-notification/push.scheduler.ts`

Description: Recovery-only scheduler for the push notification module. Same pattern as MailScheduler: When FCM is healthy, pushes are dispatched immediately. When something fails, this scheduler picks up stuck PENDING records. Uses @DistributedLock (Redis → PG advisory lock fallback).

Properties:
- `cleanupDevicesDays: number = 60`
- `cleanupOutboxDays: number = 30`
- `logger: unknown = new Logger(PushScheduler.name)`
- `stuckThresholdMinutes: number = 2`

Methods:
- `cleanup(): Promise<void>` — Cleanup old outbox records.

### RefreshTokenRepository

File: `src/modules/auth/refresh-token.repository.ts`

Description: Repository\_Layer for the refresh-token aggregate inside the Auth module. Responsibilities: Encapsulate every read/write against the refresh\_token table. Inherit the standard BaseRepository contract ( findById , findByIdOrFail , save , softDelete , count ). Expose the lookup/revoke commands the import('./service/refresh-token.service').RefreshTokenService needs for the issue / rotate / logout flows. Constraints (mirrors import('./auth.repository').AuthRepository): MUST inject Repository\<RefreshTokenEntity\> via @InjectRepository . MUST NOT inject services from other modules — cross-module access (looking up the User) is handled at the service layer. MUST NOT enforce business validation (expiry / reuse decisions stay in the service layer). "Active" here means only "not yet revoked".

Properties:
- `entityName: string = 'refresh_token'`
- `repo: Repository<TEntity>` — TypeORM repository injected by the subclass.

Methods:
- `findActiveByTokenHash(tokenHash: string): Promise<RefreshTokenEntity | null>` — Look up a not-yet-revoked token row by its SHA-256 hash. Returns null when no row matches or the matching row has been revoked. Note: expiry is intentionally NOT filtered here — deciding what to do with an expired-but-not-revoked row (reject + revoke) is a service concern.
- `revokeAllByUserId(userId: string, revokedAt: Date): Promise<void>` — Revoke every still-active token for a user (logout-everywhere). Only rows with revokedAt IS NULL are touched so prior revocation timestamps are preserved.
- `revokeById(id: string, revokedAt: Date): Promise<void>` — Mark a single token row revoked. Idempotent for an already-revoked row.
- `count(options?: FindManyOptions<TEntity>): Promise<number>` — Count rows that match the given options. The options shape mirrors TypeORM's FindManyOptions.
- `findById(id: string): Promise<TEntity | null>` — Look up an entity by its primary id. Returns null when the id does not exist (no exception thrown).
- `findByIdOrFail(id: string): Promise<TEntity>` — Same as findById but throws NotFoundException with an i18n key ( {entity}.not\_found ) when the id does not exist.
- `save(data: Partial<TEntity>): Promise<TEntity>` — Persist a partial entity. Implementations may either INSERT a new row (when id is absent) or UPDATE an existing row.
- `softDelete(id: string): Promise<void>` — Soft-delete the entity with the given id (sets deleted\_at ).

### RefreshTokenService

File: `src/modules/auth/service/refresh-token.service.ts`

Description: RefreshTokenService — owns the lifecycle of opaque (non-JWT) refresh tokens: issuance, rotation and revocation. Design: The token is an opaque high-entropy random string. The server keeps no decodable claims in it — validity is determined purely by the DB row keyed on the token's SHA-256 hash. Rotation: every successful refresh consumes (revokes) the presented token and issues a fresh one. A refresh token is therefore single-use — replaying a rotated token fails, which also surfaces token theft (the legitimate client and the attacker can't both hold a valid token). This service deliberately does NOT mint access tokens — that stays with import('./auth.service').AuthService. Keeping the dependency one-directional (AuthService → RefreshTokenService for issuance) avoids a circular module dependency; the refresh endpoint composes the two.

Methods:
- `generateRawToken(): string` — Opaque, URL-safe random token. The rt\_ prefix aids log/debug triage.
- `getTtlMs(): number` — Refresh-token TTL in ms, parsed from jwt.rfExpireTime (e.g. "360000s").
- `hashToken(rawToken: string): string` — Deterministic SHA-256 hash used as the DB lookup key.
- `issueForUser(userId: string, meta: RefreshTokenMeta = {}): Promise<IssuedRefreshToken>` — Issue a brand-new refresh token for a user and persist its hash. Returns the raw token (shown once) plus its expiry.
- `resolveActive(rawToken: string): Promise<RefreshTokenEntity>` — Resolve a raw token to its active, unexpired row. An expired (but not yet revoked) row is revoked on the spot before rejecting, so it can't be retried.
- `revoke(rawToken: string): Promise<void>` — Revoke a single refresh token (logout on the current device). Unknown or already-revoked tokens are treated as a no-op — logout is idempotent and must not leak whether a token existed.
- `revokeAllForUser(userId: string): Promise<void>` — Revoke every active refresh token for a user (logout everywhere).
- `rotate(rawToken: string, meta: RefreshTokenMeta = {}): Promise<IssuedRefreshToken>` — Rotate a refresh token: validate the presented one, revoke it, and issue a replacement bound to the same user. Throws UnauthorizedException when the token is unknown, already rotated/revoked, or expired. Policy: when jwt.rotateRefreshToken is false , rotation is disabled — the presented token is validated and returned as-is (only the access token is refreshed). This trades away single-use theft detection for a longer-lived, reusable refresh token.

### SnowflakeAllocatorService

File: `src/modules/shared/services/snowflake-allocator.service.ts`

Description: Allocates a unique Snowflake instance\_id per pod via a DB-backed lease, replacing the random fallback used during local development. Why: random ids are 12-bit, so on ECS/EKS with many pods restarting there's a non-trivial probability of two pods picking the same id and silently emitting duplicate Snowflake IDs. A DB lease guarantees exclusivity for the lifetime of the pod. Implementation notes: We acquire a Postgres session-level advisory lock around the slot selection so concurrent boots don't race on the same row. The lease is renewed by a heartbeat that extends expires\_at . If the heartbeat ever finds its row hijacked (different holder ), it re-acquires a fresh slot — that path is rare but covers split-brain after long pauses (network partitions, host suspends, etc.). On graceful shutdown we set expires\_at = now() so the slot is immediately reclaimable. Hard kills fall back to TTL expiry.

Properties:
- `heartbeatMs: number`
- `heartbeatTimer: NodeJS.Timeout | null = null`
- `holder: string`
- `instanceId: number | null = null`
- `leaseMs: number`
- `logger: unknown = new Logger(SnowflakeAllocatorService.name)`

Methods:
- `acquireSlot(): Promise<number>` — Atomically pick the lowest free instance\_id and write a lease row for it. The advisory lock serializes concurrent pods so two of them can't both observe the same slot as free.
- `acquireWithRetry(): Promise<number>`
- `getInstanceId(): number | null` — Exposed for diagnostics / health checks.
- `heartbeat(): Promise<void>`
- `onApplicationBootstrap(): Promise<void>`
- `onApplicationShutdown(): Promise<void>`
- `startHeartbeat(): void`
- `stopHeartbeat(): void`

### SocialService

File: `src/modules/auth/service/social.service.ts`

Description: SocialService — verifies third-party ID tokens (Apple, LINE) and resolves them to a stable SocialIdentity. Apple tokens are RS256 JWTs verified locally against Apple's published JWKS using WebCrypto. LINE tokens are verified through LINE's /oauth2/v2.1/verify endpoint, which validates the signature, expiry and audience server-side.

Properties:
- `appleJwksCache?: { keys: JwkWithKid[]; fetchedAt: number }`
- `logger: unknown = new Logger(SocialService.name)`

Methods:
- `assertAppleClaims(payload: ApplePayload): void` — Validate the issuer, audience and expiry claims of an Apple ID token.
- `base64UrlDecode(value: string): Buffer`
- `decodeJwt(token: string): { header: JwtHeader; payload: T; signedData: Uint8Array; signature: Uint8Array }` — Split and decode a compact JWS, returning header, payload and raw bytes.
- `fail(reason: string): never` — Log the real reason (for ops/debugging) but never leak it to the client — every failure surfaces the same generic SOCIAL\_LOGIN\_FAILED key.
- `fetchAppleJwks(): Promise<JwkWithKid[]>`
- `getAppleJwk(kid: string): Promise<JwkWithKid>` — Resolve the Apple signing key matching kid , refreshing JWKS on miss.
- `getDumpSocialProfile(jwtTokenDump: string): unknown`
- `isExpired(exp: number): boolean`
- `isJwksStale(): boolean`
- `requestLineVerify(idToken: string, channelId: string): Promise<LineVerifyResponse>` — Call LINE's verify endpoint and return the validated payload.
- `verifyApple(idToken: string): Promise<SocialIdentity>`
- `verifyIdToken(provider: SocialProvider, idToken: string): Promise<SocialIdentity>` — Verify an ID token for the given provider and return the identity.
- `verifyLine(idToken: string): Promise<SocialIdentity>`
- `verifyRs256(jwk: JsonWebKey, signedData: Uint8Array, signature: Uint8Array): Promise<boolean>` — Verify an RS256 signature over signedData using a JWK public key.

### UserRepository

File: `src/modules/user/user.repository.ts`

Description: Repository\_Layer for the User aggregate. Responsibilities: Encapsulate every read/write against the user table. Inherit the standard BaseRepository contract ( findById , findByIdOrFail , save , softDelete , count ). Expose User-specific query methods used by UserService and other Complex\_Business\_Module services that need to look up users via the User module's public surface. Constraints (per design / Requirements 3.x and 12.x): MUST inject Repository\<UserEntity\> via @InjectRepository . MUST NOT inject services from other modules. MUST NOT inject EventEmitter2 — emitting domain events is the Service layer's responsibility. MUST NOT enforce authorization or contain business validation. The entityName ("user") is used by findByIdOrFail to throw a NotFoundException with the i18n key 'user.not\_found' .

Properties:
- `entityName: string = 'user'`
- `repo: Repository<TEntity>` — TypeORM repository injected by the subclass.

Methods:
- `createUser(userRegisterDto: RegisterDto): Promise<UserEntity>`
- `createUserWithSocialAccount(userRegisterDto: RegisterDto, provider: string, providerUserId: string, providerEmail?: string): Promise<UserEntity>`
- `existsByEmail(email: string, excludeId?: string): Promise<boolean>` — Check whether a user with the given email exists. When excludeId is provided the row with that id is ignored — useful for "email unique on update" checks.
- `findActiveAdminByEmail(email: string): Promise<UserEntity | null>` — Find an active admin by email — used by AuthService.adminLogin . Returns the user with the auth-relevant columns selected (including password for hash validation).
- `findActiveLoginCandidate(email: string): Promise<UserEntity | null>` — Load an active user for the standard login flow. Returns null when the user does not exist or is not active.
- `findAdminByEmail(email: string): Promise<UserEntity | null>` — Find an admin by email regardless of isActive flag — used by AuthService.adminRequestReset . Returns null when no admin matches (callers may treat null as "no such account").
- `findAdminUsers(): Promise<UserEntity[]>` — Return all admin users.
- `findByEmail(email: string): Promise<UserEntity | null>` — Look up a user by email. Returns null when no row matches.
- `findByIdWithCompany(id: string): Promise<UserEntity | null>` — Load a user by ID. Used by AuthService.getUserInfo .
- `findManyByIds(ids: string[]): Promise<UserEntity[]>` — Bulk lookup by ids. Returns an empty array when ids is empty (avoids issuing a WHERE id IN () query that some drivers reject).
- `findSocialProfile(provider: string, providerUserId: string): Promise<UserEntity | null>` — Load a user by ID. Used by AuthService.getUserInfo .
- `findWithPagination(options: UserQueryOptions): Promise<PaginatedResult<UserEntity>>` — Paginated user listing with optional search, role and company filters. Search matches case-insensitively against fullName and email .
- `updatePassword(id: string, hashedPassword: string): Promise<void>` — Persist a new password hash for the given user. Implemented as a direct UPDATE so the operation does not load the entity first (used by password reset / change-password flows).
- `count(options?: FindManyOptions<TEntity>): Promise<number>` — Count rows that match the given options. The options shape mirrors TypeORM's FindManyOptions.
- `findById(id: string): Promise<TEntity | null>` — Look up an entity by its primary id. Returns null when the id does not exist (no exception thrown).
- `findByIdOrFail(id: string): Promise<TEntity>` — Same as findById but throws NotFoundException with an i18n key ( {entity}.not\_found ) when the id does not exist.
- `save(data: Partial<TEntity>): Promise<TEntity>` — Persist a partial entity. Implementations may either INSERT a new row (when id is absent) or UPDATE an existing row.
- `softDelete(id: string): Promise<void>` — Soft-delete the entity with the given id (sets deleted\_at ).

### AdminLoginOtpSentEvent

Description: Emitted when an OTP is dispatched to an admin user during login flow. ⚠️ SENSITIVE DATA WARNING (Requirement 6.3 violation): Payload hiện tại chứa raw otpCode . TODO(task 12.4): Refactor để loại bỏ otpCode . Validates Requirements: 6.2, 15.1, 15.2, 15.3, 15.4

### BaseBusinessService

File: `src/common/services/base-business-service.ts`

Description: Abstract base class for Complex Business Module services. Implements the Template Method pattern for create and update : create(dto) : validateCreate(dto) — business rule validation mapToEntity(dto) — DTO → entity transformation repository.save(entity) — persist emitCreatedEvent(saved) — emit domain event (only on success) update(id, dto) : repository.findByIdOrFail(id) — load existing validateUpdate(existing, dto) — business rule validation applyChanges(existing, dto) — compute updated state repository.save(updated) — persist emitUpdatedEvent(before, after) — emit domain event (only on success) Property 9 (event-after-persist): emitCreatedEvent / emitUpdatedEvent are awaited after repository.save resolves. If save throws, the emit step is never reached and no event is published. Subclasses MUST keep this invariant — never emit inside validateCreate , mapToEntity , validateUpdate , or applyChanges . TEntity - The aggregate entity (must extend WithIdAndTimestamp). TCreateDto - DTO accepted by create . TUpdateDto - DTO accepted by update .

Methods:
- `applyChanges(existing: TEntity, dto: TUpdateDto): Partial<TEntity>` — Compute the next entity state by merging dto into existing . Should return a partial entity that, when saved, produces the desired update.
- `create(dto: TCreateDto): Promise<TEntity>` — Template method for the create flow. Order of operations is fixed by this base class to guarantee Property 9: the domain event is emitted only after repository.save resolves successfully.
- `emitCreatedEvent(entity: TEntity): Promise<void>` — Emit the domain event corresponding to a successful create. Called AFTER repository.save resolves (Property 9).
- `emitUpdatedEvent(before: TEntity, after: TEntity): Promise<void>` — Emit the domain event corresponding to a successful update. Called AFTER repository.save resolves (Property 9). Receives both the pre-update ( before ) and post-update ( after ) snapshots so subclasses can include diff information in the event payload if needed.
- `mapToEntity(dto: TCreateDto): Partial<TEntity>` — Map a create DTO to a partial entity ready for repository.save . Implementations MUST NOT perform I/O here — keep this pure.
- `update(id: string, dto: TUpdateDto): Promise<TEntity>` — Template method for the update flow. Same Property 9 guarantee applies: emitUpdatedEvent runs only after repository.save resolves successfully.
- `validateCreate(dto: TCreateDto): Promise<void>` — Validate the create payload against business rules (uniqueness, capacity, referenced ids existing, etc). Throw a NestJS HTTP exception to abort persistence.
- `validateUpdate(existing: TEntity, dto: TUpdateDto): Promise<void>` — Validate the update payload against the existing entity (state transitions, ownership, etc). Throw a NestJS HTTP exception to abort persistence.

### BaseOutboxService

File: `libs/infrastructure/messaging/outbox/base-outbox.service.ts`

Description: Abstract base class for outbox services. Provides CRUD + recovery operations for the transactional outbox pattern. Retry timing is handled externally: BullMQ mode: BullMQ built-in retry + backoff. Direct mode: Scheduler polls getStuckPending() every 30s. Permanent errors (invalid email, unregistered token) skip retry entirely. Usage: @Injectable() class OutboxEmailService extends BaseOutboxService { constructor(@InjectRepository(OutboxEmail) repo: Repository ) { super(repo); } }

Properties:
- `logger: unknown = new Logger(this.constructor.name)`

Methods:
- `cleanup(days: unknown = DEFAULT_CLEANUP_DAYS): Promise<number>` — Delete old sent or permanently-failed records.
- `createPending(data: Partial<T>): Promise<T>` — Create a new pending outbox record.
- `getPendingBatch(limit: unknown = DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE): Promise<T[]>` — Get a batch of pending records ready for dispatch. Filters records where nextRetryAt is null or in the past.
- `getStuckPending(minutes: number): Promise<T[]>` — Get records stuck in PENDING state for longer than the specified duration. Used by the scheduler for recovery when BullMQ/Redis is unavailable.
- `markFailed(id: string, error: string, permanent: unknown = false, patch?: Partial<T>): Promise<void>` — Mark a record as failed. Example : Use for permanent errors: invalid email, token not registered. Default false → keeps PENDING for scheduler retry. saved even though dispatch failed so the row reflects what was built.
- `markSent(id: string, patch?: Partial<T>): Promise<void>` — Mark a record as successfully sent. Uses TypeORM increment() — safe from SQL injection.

### BaseRepository

File: `src/common/repositories/base.repository.ts`

Description: Optional abstract base class that module-level repositories MAY extend to inherit a default implementation of the IBaseRepository contract. Subclasses only have to provide: A TypeORM Repository via the repo property (typically injected with @InjectRepository(Entity) ). An entityName string that becomes the i18n prefix for findByIdOrFail errors (for example, 'user' produces the i18n key 'user.not\_found' ). Module repositories are free to override any method to add module-specific behavior, or to skip this base class entirely and implement IBaseRepository directly. Example: Example : &#64;Injectable() export class UserRepository extends BaseRepository\<UserEntity\> { protected readonly entityName = 'user'; constructor( &#64;InjectRepository(UserEntity) protected readonly repo: Repository\<UserEntity\>, ) { super(); } findByEmail(email: string) { return this.repo.findOneBy({ email }); } }

Properties:
- `entityName: string` — i18n prefix used for not-found errors. Subclasses MUST override this with the aggregate name (e.g. 'user' , 'insurance\_contract' ).
- `repo: Repository<TEntity>` — TypeORM repository injected by the subclass.

Methods:
- `count(options?: FindManyOptions<TEntity>): Promise<number>` — Count rows that match the given options. The options shape mirrors TypeORM's FindManyOptions.
- `findById(id: string): Promise<TEntity | null>` — Look up an entity by its primary id. Returns null when the id does not exist (no exception thrown).
- `findByIdOrFail(id: string): Promise<TEntity>` — Same as findById but throws NotFoundException with an i18n key ( {entity}.not\_found ) when the id does not exist.
- `save(data: Partial<TEntity>): Promise<TEntity>` — Persist a partial entity. Implementations may either INSERT a new row (when id is absent) or UPDATE an existing row.
- `softDelete(id: string): Promise<void>` — Soft-delete the entity with the given id (sets deleted\_at ).

### ConversationGateway

File: `src/modules/conversation/conversation.gateway.ts`

Properties:
- `logger: unknown = new Logger(ConversationGateway.name)`
- `MAX_CONNECTIONS_PER_USER: number = 5` — Maximum concurrent connections per user
- `MAX_INITIAL_ROOMS: number = 100` — Maximum number of group rooms to join on initial connection
- `server: Server`

Methods:
- `emitToGroup(groupId: string, event: string, payload: any): void` — Emit an event to all sockets in a group room.
- `emitToUser(userId: string, event: string, payload: any): Promise<void>` — Emit an event to all sockets of a specific user.
- `enforceConnectionLimit(client: Socket, userId: string, redisKey: string): Promise<void>` — Enforce the max connection limit per user. If the user already has MAX\_CONNECTIONS\_PER\_USER connections, disconnect the oldest one (earliest timestamp).
- `getConnectionsMap(key: string): Promise<Record<string, string>>` — Get the connections map from Redis (JSON-encoded).
- `handleConnection(client: Socket): Promise<void>` — Handle new WebSocket connection. Validate JWT from auth handshake Check connection count (max 5, disconnect oldest if exceeded) Store connection in Redis hash Join all group rooms where user is an active participant Requirements: 8.1, 8.2, 8.3, 8.4, 8.5
- `handleConversationOpened(client: Socket, payload: { groupId: string }): Promise<void>` — Handle conversation-opened event from client. Resets the unread count for the user in the specified group. Requirements: 9.6
- `handleDisconnect(client: Socket): Promise<void>` — Handle WebSocket disconnection. Remove the connection from Redis hash. Socket.IO automatically handles leaving all rooms. Requirements: 8.4, 8.5
- `handleGroupCreated(event: GroupCreatedEvent): Promise<void>` — Handle GroupCreatedEvent. Emit group:created to all participants and join their sockets to the new room. Requirements: 1.5
- `handleGroupDissolved(event: GroupDissolvedEvent): Promise<void>` — Handle GroupDissolvedEvent. Emit group:dissolved to all participants. Requirements: 7.5
- `handleGroupUpdated(event: GroupUpdatedEvent): Promise<void>` — Handle GroupUpdatedEvent. Emit group:updated to the room. Requirements: 6.1, 6.2
- `handleMemberAdded(event: MemberAddedEvent): Promise<void>` — Handle MemberAddedEvent. Emit group:member-added to the room and join the new member's sockets. Requirements: 2.4, 2.5
- `handleMemberLeft(event: MemberLeftEvent): Promise<void>` — Handle MemberLeftEvent. Emit group:member-left to the room and remove the member's sockets from the room. Requirements: 7.2
- `handleMemberRemoved(event: MemberRemovedEvent): Promise<void>` — Handle MemberRemovedEvent. Emit group:member-removed to the room and remove the member's sockets from the room. Requirements: 2.4
- `handleMessageDelivered(client: Socket, payload: { messageId: string; groupId: string }): Promise<void>` — Handle message:delivered event from client. Called when a recipient's device acknowledges receiving a message. Requirements: real-time delivery acknowledgment
- `handleMessageDeliveredEvent(event: MessageDeliveredEvent): Promise<void>` — Handle MessageDeliveredEvent. Send message:delivered to the sender to notify that a recipient received the message. Requirements: real-time delivery acknowledgment
- `handleMessageRead(client: Socket, payload: { groupId: string; messageIds?: string[] }): Promise<void>` — Handle message:read event from client. Called when a user reads one or more messages in a conversation. Requirements: real-time read acknowledgment
- `handleMessageReadEvent(event: MessageReadEvent): Promise<void>` — Handle MessageReadEvent. Send message:read to the sender to notify that a recipient read the message. Requirements: real-time read acknowledgment
- `handleMessageSent(event: MessageSentEvent): Promise<void>` — Handle MessageSentEvent. Send message:sent acknowledgment back to the sender only. This confirms the message was saved on the server and provides the server-generated ID. Requirements: real-time sent acknowledgment
- `handleNewMessage(event: NewMessageEvent): Promise<void>` — Handle NewMessageEvent. Broadcast group:new-message to the room and emit group:conversation-list-updated. Requirements: 3.4, 9.7
- `joinUserToRoom(userId: string, groupId: string): Promise<void>` — Join a specific user's sockets to a group room. Used when a user is added to a group while already connected.
- `redisHDel(key: string, field: string): Promise<void>` — Delete a field from a Redis hash (stored as JSON).
- `redisHGetAll(key: string): Promise<Record | null>` — Get all fields from a Redis hash (stored as JSON).
- `redisHSet(key: string, field: string, value: string): Promise<void>` — Set a field in a Redis hash. Uses the underlying Redis instance via eval-like approach with setValue. Since RedisCacheService doesn't expose hash commands directly, we store as a JSON-encoded value under the key.
- `removeUserFromRoom(userId: string, groupId: string): Promise<void>` — Remove a specific user's sockets from a group room. Used when a user is removed from or leaves a group.

### DomainEvent

File: `src/common/events/domain-event.base.ts`

Description: Abstract base class cho tất cả domain events. Mọi concrete event class: PHẢI declare static readonly eventName: string tuân theo EVENT\_NAME\_REGEX . PHẢI declare các payload field là readonly (immutability). PHẢI có constructor nhận đầy đủ các trường bắt buộc của payload. KHÔNG được chứa các field nhạy cảm: password , passwordHash , accessToken , refreshToken , otpCode . occurredAt được auto-populate tại thời điểm event được khởi tạo, dùng cho audit trail và ordering. Example : export class UserCreatedEvent extends DomainEvent { static readonly eventName = 'user.created'; \_\_\_COMPODOC\_EMPTY\_LINE\_\_\_ constructor( public readonly userId: string, public readonly companyId: string, ) { super(); } }

Properties:
- `eventName: string` — Canonical event name, override trong concrete class. TypeScript không hỗ trợ abstract static , nên field này được khai báo như một contract bằng convention. Concrete class PHẢI override.
- `occurredAt: Date` — Thời điểm event được khởi tạo (UTC).

### LockManager

File: `libs/infrastructure/lock/lock-manager.ts`

Description: LockManager orchestrates distributed lock acquisition across multiple adapters with automatic fallback. Usage: const manager = new LockManager({ adapters: \[redisAdapter, postgresAdapter\], }); // The manager tries Redis first; if Redis is down, falls back to PG. const released = await manager.withLock('my-job', async () =\> { // critical section });

Properties:
- `adapters: LockAdapter[]`
- `defaultOnFail: "skip" | "throw"`
- `defaultTtlMs: number`
- `lockOwnership: unknown = new Map<string, LockAdapter>()` — Track which adapter holds which lock for correct release
- `logger: unknown = new Logger('LockManager')`

Methods:
- `acquire(options: LockOptions): Promise<boolean>` — Acquire a lock using the first healthy adapter. Falls back to subsequent adapters if the primary is unavailable.
- `release(key: string): Promise<boolean>` — Release a previously acquired lock.
- `resolveOptions(key: string, partial?: Partial<LockOptions>): LockOptions`
- `shutdown(): Promise<void>` — Gracefully shut down all adapters.
- `sleep(ms: number): Promise<void>`
- `tryAcquireOnce(key: string, ttlMs?: number): Promise<boolean>`
- `withLock(key: string, fn: function, options?: Partial<LockOptions>): Promise<T | undefined>` — Acquire a lock, execute the callback, then release. Returns the callback result, or undefined if lock was not acquired (onFail: 'skip').

### LockNotAcquiredError

Extends: `Error`

### LoggingExceptionFilter

File: `libs/infrastructure/logging/logging-exception.filter.ts`

Methods:

- `extractMessage(exception: unknown): string` — Extracts the raw, untranslated message from any thrown value. This value doubles as the i18n key and the errorCode returned to the client.
- `translate(key: string, lang?: string): Promise<string>`

### PostgresLockAdapter

File: `libs/infrastructure/lock/adapters/postgres-lock.adapter.ts`

Description: PostgreSQL advisory lock adapter. Uses pg\_try\_advisory\_lock / pg\_advisory\_unlock for non-blocking distributed locking. Note: PG advisory locks don't have native TTL — the lock is held until explicitly released or the session disconnects.

Properties:
- `activeLocks: unknown = new Map<string, QueryRunner>()` — Track active locks: key → QueryRunner (needed for release)
- `logger: unknown = new Logger('PostgresLockAdapter')`
- `name: string = 'postgres'`

Methods:
- `acquire(key: string, _ttlMs?: number): Promise<boolean>`
- `getDataSource(): DataSource | null`
- `isHealthy(): Promise<boolean>`
- `release(key: string): Promise<boolean>`
- `shutdown(): Promise<void>`

### RedisIoAdapter

Extends: `IoAdapter`

- `logger: unknown = new Logger('RedisIoAdapter')`

Methods:
- `connectToRedis(config: WebSocketAdapterConfig): Promise<void>` — Connect to Redis for Socket.IO pub/sub. If Redis is unavailable, falls back to PostgreSQL LISTEN/NOTIFY. If both are unavailable, uses the default in-memory adapter (single-node only).
- `createIOServer(port: number, options?: Partial<ServerOptions>): any`
- `tryPostgresAdapter(databaseUrl: string): Promise<boolean>`
- `tryRedisAdapter(redisConfig: RedisConfig): Promise<boolean>`

### RedisLockAdapter

File: `libs/infrastructure/lock/adapters/redis-lock.adapter.ts`

Description: Redis distributed lock adapter. Uses SET key value NX PX ttl pattern (single-instance Redlock). For production multi-node Redis, consider extending with full Redlock algorithm. Requires an ioredis instance to be provided via configure().

Properties:
- `activeLocks: unknown = new Map<string, string>()` — Unique value per lock to ensure only the holder can release
- `logger: unknown = new Logger('RedisLockAdapter')`
- `name: string = 'redis'`
- `redisClient: any | null = null`

Methods:
- `acquire(key: string, ttlMs: number = 30000): Promise<boolean>`
- `buildKey(key: string): string`
- `configure(redisClient: any): void` — Configure the adapter with an ioredis client instance. Must be called before acquire/release.
- `generateValue(): string`
- `isHealthy(): Promise<boolean>`
- `release(key: string): Promise<boolean>`
- `shutdown(): Promise<void>`

### S3StorageProvider

File: `src/modules/storage/providers/s3-storage.provider.ts`

Properties:
- `bucket: string`
- `logger: unknown = new Logger(S3StorageProvider.name)`
- `prefix: string` — Prefix for private objects — all presigned upload/get/delete flows use this.
- `publicPrefix: string` — Prefix for public objects — readable directly via getPublicUrl without signing.
- `region: string`
- `s3: S3Client`

Methods:
- `buildClientConfig(): S3ClientConfig` — Builds the S3 client config. When aws.endpoint is set (local S3-compatible storage such as RustFS or MinIO), it points the client at that endpoint, forces path-style URLs (compatible servers don't support virtual-hosted-style buckets) and passes explicit credentials. When unset, the client falls back to the standard AWS default credential chain + real S3 endpoint — so production is unchanged.
- `deleteFile(key: string): Promise<void>`
- `deleteFiles(keys: string[]): Promise<void>`
- `getFileUrl(key: string): Promise<string>`
- `getPresignedGetUrls(keys: string[], expiresIn: number = 300): Promise<Record<string, string>>`
- `getPresignedPostUrl(filename: string, options?: { contentType?: string; expiresIn?: number }): Promise<{ uploadUrl: string; fields: Record<string, string>; fileUrl: string }>`
- `getPresignedPutUrl(filename: string, options?: { contentType?: string; expiresIn?: number }): Promise<{ uploadUrl: string; fileUrl: string }>`
- `getPresignedUploadUrl(filename: string, options?: { contentType?: string; expiresIn?: number }): Promise<{ uploadUrl: string; fileUrl: string; fields?: Record<string, string> }>`
- `getPublicUrl(key: string): string` — Builds a direct, unsigned, permanent URL for a public object. Only objects stored under the public prefix (and covered by the bucket's public-read policy) are actually reachable this way. Use this instead of a presigned URL for files that don't need access control.
- `getRequiredConfig(key: string): string`

### SendEmailOtpDto

### SendMessageDto

File: `src/modules/conversation/dtos/request/send-message.dto.ts`

Properties:
- `clientMessageId: string`

### TokenBucket

File: `libs/infrastructure/utils/token-bucket.ts`

Description: In-memory Token Bucket rate limiter. Enforces a maximum request rate without any external dependency (no Redis). Used as the ultimate fallback rate-limit layer in dispatchers (Email, FCM, etc.) to guarantee third-party API rate limits are never exceeded — even when Redis/BullMQ are down. Usage: const bucket = new TokenBucket({ rate: 14, burst: 14 }); await bucket.waitForToken(); // blocks until a token is available // ... make the rate-limited API call

Properties:
- `burst: number`
- `lastRefill: number`
- `maxQueueSize: number`
- `rate: number`
- `tokens: number`
- `waitQueue: Array<void> = []` — Pending resolvers waiting for tokens

Methods:
- `drainQueue(): void` — Drain the wait queue as tokens become available.
- `refill(): void` — Refill tokens based on elapsed time.
- `waitForToken(): Promise<void>` — Wait until a token is available, then consume it. Uses a refill-then-drain strategy: Refill tokens based on elapsed time since last refill. If a token is available, consume and return immediately. Otherwise, queue the caller and resolve when a token becomes available.

### TypeOrmLoggerService

File: `libs/infrastructure/logging/typeorm-logger.service.ts`

Description: Custom TypeORM Logger that integrates with the application's LoggingService. All logs are routed through LoggingService to benefit from: Structured JSON logging Correlation ID propagation Sensitive field redaction Console output Additionally, SQL queries are written to a separate daily-rotated file ( logs/sql-YYYY-MM-DD.log ) for easy inspection.

Properties:
- `sqlFileLogger: winston.Logger | null = null`

Methods:
- `createSqlFileLogger(): winston.Logger` — Creates a dedicated Winston logger that writes SQL queries to a daily-rotated file (logs/sql-YYYY-MM-DD.log).
- `ensureLogDir(dirPath: string): boolean` — Ensures the log directory exists, creating it recursively if needed.
- `log(level: "log" | "info" | "warn", message: any, _queryRunner?: QueryRunner): void`
- `logMigration(message: string, _queryRunner?: QueryRunner): void`
- `logQuery(query: string, parameters?: any[], _queryRunner?: QueryRunner): void`
- `logQueryError(error: string | Error, query: string, parameters?: any[], _queryRunner?: QueryRunner): void`
- `logQuerySlow(time: number, query: string, parameters?: any[], _queryRunner?: QueryRunner): void`
- `logSchemaBuild(message: string, _queryRunner?: QueryRunner): void`
- `writeSqlFile(type: string, message: string, parameters?: any[], error?: string, time?: number): void` — Writes a log entry to the dedicated SQL file logger (if enabled).

### VerifyOtpResponseDto

File: `src/modules/auth/dto/otp/otp-response.dto.ts`

Description: Response returned after a successful OTP verification. The shape is purpose-dependent (the endpoint is shared): LOGIN\_VERIFY : the OTP completes a login — a full session is issued ( accessToken + refreshToken + data user), same as a direct login. PASSWORD\_RESET / EMAIL\_VERIFY : only a short-lived accessToken carrying the identifier + email claims (the next-step exchange credential). In both cases the OTP record is consumed (hard-deleted).

Properties:
- `accessToken: string`
- `data?: UserEntity`
- `refreshToken?: string`
- `refreshTokenExpiresAt?: Date`

### BaseBusinessRepository

File: `src/common/services/base-business-service.ts`

Description: Minimal structural contract that BaseBusinessService relies on. The full BaseRepository contract (with findById , softDelete , count , etc.) is defined separately by task 1.4 in src/common/repositories/base.repository.ts . Any concrete repository that implements that fuller contract is structurally assignable to this one, which keeps BaseBusinessService decoupled from the repository module.

Methods:
- `findByIdOrFail(id: string): Promise<TEntity>` — Load an entity by id, throwing NotFoundException (with i18n key) when the id is not found. Used by BaseBusinessService.update before applying changes.
- `save(data: Partial<TEntity>): Promise<TEntity>` — Persist the given (partial) entity and resolve with the saved entity, including database-generated fields (id, timestamps).

### CursorPaginationInput

File: `src/modules/conversation/repositories/contracts/pagination.ts`

Description: Input for cursor-paginated list endpoints. cursor is the exclusive lower bound (a Snowflake ID string). pageSize defaults to 20 and is clamped to \[1, 100\].

Properties:
- `cursor?: string` — Exclusive cursor — return items with id \< cursor (Snowflake DESC order)
- `pageSize?: number` — Number of items per page (1–100, default 20 or 50 depending on endpoint)

### IBaseRepository

File: `src/common/repositories/base.repository.ts`

Description: Standard contract that every Complex\_Business\_Module repository must satisfy. The methods listed here are the minimum surface area that service layers can rely on when interacting with persistence. Implementations: MUST NOT enforce authorization (that is the service/guard layer's job). MUST NOT contain business validation logic. MUST NOT emit domain events. See: Requirements 12.1, 12.2, 12.3, 12.5

Methods:
- `count(options?: FindManyOptions<TEntity>): Promise<number>` — Count rows that match the given options. The options shape mirrors TypeORM's FindManyOptions.
- `findById(id: string): Promise<TEntity | null>` — Look up an entity by its primary id. Returns null when the id does not exist (no exception thrown).
- `findByIdOrFail(id: string): Promise<TEntity>` — Same as findById but throws NotFoundException with an i18n key ( {entity}.not\_found ) when the id does not exist.
- `save(data: Partial<TEntity>): Promise<TEntity>` — Persist a partial entity. Implementations may either INSERT a new row (when id is absent) or UPDATE an existing row.
- `softDelete(id: string): Promise<void>` — Soft-delete the entity with the given id (sets deleted\_at ).

### IEmailDispatcher

File: `src/modules/email/email-dispatcher.interface.ts`
Extends: `IMessageDispatcher<EmailJob>`

Description: Email-specific dispatcher interface. See EmailJob for the payload shape. When BullMQ is integrated: Create a BullMqEmailDispatcher that implements this interface. The dispatcher pushes EmailJob to BullMQ (tiny payload: ~100 bytes vs ~100KB HTML). A BullMQ Worker consumes the job, renders, and sends via SmtpEmailDispatcher. Usage in module: { provide: EMAIL\_DISPATCHER, useClass: SmtpEmailDispatcher } // Swap to BullMQ later: // { provide: EMAIL\_DISPATCHER, useClass: BullMqEmailDispatcher }

Methods:
- `dispatch(message: TMessage): Promise<DispatchResult>` — Dispatch a message through the channel.

Methods:
- `check(): Promise<DependencyHealth>` — Check the health of this dependency. Must NEVER throw — all errors are captured in DependencyHealth.

### IMessageDispatcher

File: `libs/infrastructure/messaging/interfaces/message-dispatcher.interface.ts`

Methods:
- `dispatch(message: TMessage): Promise<DispatchResult>` — Dispatch a message through the channel.

### IMessageRenderer

File: `libs/infrastructure/messaging/interfaces/message-renderer.interface.ts`

Description: Shared messaging renderer interface. Converts a template + data into the final message payload for a channel. Pure function — no DB/Redis access, no side effects. Channels: Email: template + data → { subject: string; html: string } Push: template + data → { title: string; body: string; data?: object }

Methods:
- `render(template: unknown, data: TData): Promise<TOutput>` — Render a template with the provided data into the channel-specific payload.

### IOutboxRecord

File: `libs/infrastructure/messaging/outbox/outbox-record.interface.ts`

Description: Contract that every outbox entity must satisfy to work with BaseOutboxService. Each channel (Email, Push) has its own entity that extends their base entity and also implements this interface.

Properties:
- `createdAt: Date` — Record creation timestamp
- `id: string`
- `lastAttemptAt: Date | null` — Timestamp of the last dispatch attempt
- `lastError: string | null` — Error message from the last failed attempt
- `maxRetries: number` — Maximum number of retries before marking as PERMANENTLY\_FAILED
- `nextRetryAt: Date | null` — When the next retry should occur. Calculated by exponential backoff. null means it's ready for immediate dispatch.
- `status: OutboxStatus` — Current status of this outbox record
- `tryCount: number` — Number of dispatch attempts so far

### IPushDispatcher

File: `src/modules/push-notification/push-dispatcher.interface.ts`
Extends: `IMessageDispatcher<FcmPayload>`

Description: Push notification dispatcher interface. Extends the generic IMessageDispatcher with the FcmPayload. When BullMQ is integrated later: Create a BullMqPushDispatcher that implements this interface. Swap useClass in the module.

Methods:
- `dispatch(message: TMessage): Promise<DispatchResult>` — Dispatch a message through the channel.

### LockAdapter

File: `libs/infrastructure/lock/interfaces/lock-adapter.interface.ts`

Description: Contract for distributed lock adapters. Each adapter implements acquire/release using a specific backend (PostgreSQL advisory locks, Redis SET NX, etc.)

Properties:
- `name: string` — Unique name identifying this adapter (e.g. 'postgres', 'redis')

Methods:
- `acquire(key: string, ttlMs?: number): Promise<boolean>` — Attempt to acquire the lock. Some backends (PG advisory) don't support TTL natively — adapters may ignore this or implement a best-effort timeout.
- `isHealthy(): Promise<boolean>` — Check if this adapter is currently healthy and usable. Used by LockManager to skip unhealthy adapters during fallback.
- `release(key: string): Promise<boolean>` — Release the lock.
- `shutdown(): Promise<void>` — Gracefully shut down the adapter (close connections, etc.)

### LockManagerConfig

File: `libs/infrastructure/lock/lock-manager.ts`

Properties:
- `adapters: LockAdapter[]` — Ordered list of adapters. The first healthy adapter wins. If the primary fails, it falls back to the next one.
- `defaultOnFail?: "skip" | "throw"` — Default behavior when lock cannot be acquired. 'skip'
- `defaultTtlMs?: number` — Default TTL for locks in milliseconds. 30000

### LockOptions

File: `libs/infrastructure/lock/interfaces/lock-options.interface.ts`

Properties:
- `key: string` — Unique key identifying the lock. For PG adapter, this will be hashed to a bigint. For Redis adapter, this is used as the Redis key directly.
- `onFail?: "skip" | "throw"` — What to do when the lock cannot be acquired: 'skip': silently return undefined (current behavior) 'throw': throw a LockNotAcquiredError 'skip'
- `retryIntervalMs?: number` — Retry interval when waitMs \> 0. 100
- `ttlMs?: number` — Time-to-live in milliseconds. After this duration the lock is automatically released as a safety net against deadlocks. 30000 (30 seconds)
- `waitMs?: number` — Maximum time to wait for the lock before giving up (non-blocking by default). If 0 or undefined, the lock attempt is non-blocking (try once, skip if busy). 0

### ModuleMetadata

File: `src/common/utils/module-classifier.ts`

Description: Complexity indicators describing a module's characteristics. Each boolean field represents one signal that the module exhibits non-trivial business behavior. The classifier counts how many of these are true and applies a threshold rule.

Properties:
- `emitsDomainEvents: boolean` — Service emits domain events via EventEmitter2 .
- `hasCrossModuleDeps: boolean` — Module depends on more than one other feature module.
- `hasCustomBusinessLogic: boolean` — Service exposes methods beyond standard CRUD (find/create/update/delete).
- `hasCustomValidation: boolean` — Service performs validation beyond class-validator decorators.
- `hasStateMachine: boolean` — Entity has a status field with explicit transition logic.
- `hasWorkflow: boolean` — Module implements a multi-step process / workflow.

### RetryOptions

File: `libs/common/retry/retry.util.ts`

Description: Retry utility with exponential backoff. No external dependencies — uses only built-in timers.

Properties:
- `backoffFactor?: number` — Multiplier applied to delay after each retry. Default: 2
- `initialDelayMs?: number` — Initial delay in ms before first retry. Default: 200
- `maxAttempts?: number` — Maximum number of attempts (including the first call). Default: 3
- `maxDelayMs?: number` — Maximum delay in ms between retries. Default: 10000
- `onRetry?: function` — Called on each retry with attempt number and error
- `retryIf?: function` — Optional predicate to decide if the error is retryable. Default: always retry

- `getPresignedPutUrl(filename: string, options?: { contentType?: string; expiresIn?: number }): Promise<{ uploadUrl: string; fileUrl: string }>` — Generate a pre-signed PUT upload URL. Unlike getPresignedUploadUrl (POST with form fields), the client uploads the raw body with a single HTTP PUT to uploadUrl — no multipart form. Simpler for clients that can't build a multipart request.
- `getPresignedUploadUrl(filename: string, options?: { contentType?: string; expiresIn?: number }): Promise<{ uploadUrl: string; fileUrl: string; fields?: Record<string, string> }>` — Generate a pre-signed upload URL

### UpsertOtpInput

File: `src/modules/auth/auth.repository.ts`

Description: Shape accepted by AuthRepository.upsertOtp. Mirrors the columns the AuthService currently writes through TypeORM's upsert(...) call: the row is inserted on first use and replaced (by userId conflict path) on subsequent OTP requests for the same user. The repository accepts the data as a plain object — generating the snowflake id, expiration and other defaults remains the Service layer's responsibility.

Properties:
- `deletedAt?: Date | null` — Pass null to revive a soft-deleted row when reissuing an OTP.
- `expiredAt: Date` — Wall-clock expiration timestamp.
- `identifier: string` — Opaque identifier returned to the client to correlate verify calls.
- `isUsed?: boolean` — Whether the OTP has already been consumed (defaults to false ).
- `meta?: Record<string, any>` — Free-form context persisted alongside the OTP (e.g. { email } ).
- `otp: string` — Six-digit numeric OTP shown to the user.
- `purpose: OtpPurpose` — Purpose of the OTP (login vs password reset).
- `userId: string` — Owning user id. The unique constraint on this column drives the upsert.

- `search?: string` — Optional case-insensitive substring matched against fullName and email.

## Public type aliases

- `type EmailJob = literal type | literal type` — Raw email job — contains EITHER a template reference OR already-rendered content. Design: HTTP server NEVER renders EJS. It pushes raw data to the dispatcher. The dispatcher (SmtpEmailDispatcher or BullMqEmailDispatcher) handles rendering. type: 'template' → dispatcher looks up template, renders EJS, sends. type: 'custom' → dispatcher sends the already-provided subject/html directly. When BullMQ is active, the Worker process handles the CPU-bound EJS rendering, keeping the HTTP server lightweight.
- `type JwkWithKid = JsonWebKey & literal type` — A JWK as published in a JWKS, carrying the key id we match on.
- `type MailEventName = keyof typeof MAIL_EVENT_MAP` — Union type of all registered mail event names
- `type ModuleClassification = "simple-crud" | "complex-business"` — Module classification outcome.
- `type PushEventName = keyof typeof PUSH_EVENT_MAP` — Union type of all registered push event names
- `type PushJob = literal type | literal type` — Raw push job — contains EITHER a template reference OR already-rendered content. Mirrors EmailJob pattern. The worker process handles CPU-bound EJS rendering, keeping the HTTP server lightweight. type: 'template' → worker looks up template, renders EJS, gets user devices, sends. type: 'custom' → worker sends the already-provided title/body directly.
- `type QueueName = typeof QUEUE['keyof typeof QUEUE']`
- `type RequestInterceptor = function`
- `type ResponseInterceptor = function`
- `type Result = OkResult<T> | ErrResult<E>` — Result pattern — a type-safe alternative to throwing exceptions. Inspired by Rust's Result\<T, E\> type.
- `type WorkerProcessor = function`
